text:
alex: heads up — CloudWatch anomaly: service-account 'ingest-worker-sa' used from an IP in AZ eu-west-1 at 04:12 UTC, plus I found a copy of its key in a public S3 backup. I disabled the key immediately. tagging @ops-oncall @maria for triage
sec-bot: [AUTOMATED] IAM anomaly detected: access_key AKIA... associated with ingest-worker-sa showed 12 API calls in 3m from 54.93.0.0/16. Alert id sec-202603-8472.
maria: thanks alex. can you paste the exact S3 path you saw? we need to snapshot it before we change anything.
alex: s3://redwood-backups/old/2023-07/ingest-sa.txt (public-read). contains: `ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAEXAMPLE
SECRET=verybadsecret`
samir: if it's public read then prob exfil already. good call disabling. next steps: 1) confirm no active long-lived sessions, 2) rotate the SA keys, 3) invalidate any tokens derived from it, 4) search request logs for that access key id.
ops-oncall: running queries now. sharing preliminary: Count of requests using AKIAEXAMPLE -> 162 in last 48h, primarily to /v1/ingest and s3:PutObject to customer-buckets-prod.
jess: whoa. putobject to customer buckets is high risk. need to know which buckets and whether any customer PII downloaded.
maria: I'm starting an inventory: mapping access_key -> principal -> attached policies (via `aws iam get-access-key-last-used` + `aws iam list-attached-user-policies`). also checking CloudTrail for s3:GetObject events with that key.
alex: quick containment commands I ran:
```bash
# disabled current access key
aws iam update-access-key --user-name ingest-worker-sa --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE --status Inactive
# revoke STS sessions for role (approx)
aws sts revoke-session --session-id <session-id> || echo "no session api"
```
(we don't have revoke-session in all clouds; I listed what I could)
samir: for Azure/GCP equivalents: rotate service account creds and remove bindings. Also rotate any KMS envelope keys used by the ingest pipeline — even if symmetric KMS key not exfil, ephemeral creds were used to wrap data.
jess: question: did the SA have access to production KMS CMK? check key policy. if so, we should rotate and schedule re-encryption for any sensitive objects.
maria: CMK policy check: ingest-worker-sa had Encrypt/Decrypt permissions on kms-key-arn:arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd. I'm starting a re-encryption plan for bucket objects that were touched. tagging @samir for help on rewrap.
ops-oncall: I'm running a log search to enumerate customer buckets touched and producing a minimal impact list. so far 8 unique customer buckets had PutObject from that key.
sec-bot: [SUGGESTION] Run the following SAFER quick checks: 1) `cloudtrail` filter for `GetObject` 2) `s3 access logs` for HTTP 200 to customer buckets 3) `vpc flow logs` for exfil patterns 4) heartbeats for dedicated hosts.
alex: communication: we need an incident comms stub for legal/compliance. Drafting a one-paragraph for in-house first, then will escalate if we see confirmed PII access.
samir: containment checklist I'm doing: rotate all ingest-worker-sa keys, rotate any KMS CMKs that SA could use, add deny policy on customer bucket write for that SA, and add alert rule for access-key usage from new IP ranges.
jess: post-incident controls I recommend: 1) enforce short-lived ephemeral creds for service accounts, 2) disallow persistent keys in backups via lifecycle rule and S3 block public access on backup buckets, 3) add pre-commit hook scanning for creds in repos/backups, 4) require KMS envelope key rotation every 90 days.
maria: also enabling audit logging to our central KMS-backed logging bucket with immutable retention for 1yr. will add an alert to the console when KMS decrypt is performed by unusual principal.
ops-oncall: update: bucket list attached — sending to #incidents-private. will put minimal customer list in incident doc. no confirmed downloads of GetObject yet, only PutObject events recorded.
alex: next actions assigned: samir (CMK rotation + rewrap plan), maria (log forensic + CloudTrail search), ops-oncall (customer impact list + communications), jess (policy + RBAC hardening PR), alex (comms draft + coordinate legal). plan sync in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: quick forensic snippet I used to find PutObject events: 
```text
2026-03-20T04:13:21Z s3.amazonaws.com PutObject bucket=customer-foo key=uploads/xyz size=2048 principal=ingest-worker-sa access_key=AKIAEXAMPLE
```
jess: add a monitoring alert to fire when the same access key performs PutObject to >3 distinct customer buckets in 1h.
samir: agreed. also add a rule to auto-disable keys that show geo anomaly (sign-in from country not in allowlist).
alex: thanks everyone. once we confirm no downloads of GetObject on customer buckets we'll decide whether to notify affected customers and legal. for now incident severity = P2 until confirmed exfil. will update thread with timeline and final postmortem action items. :white_check_mark:
